title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 284
paragraphs: For some of the Egyptians the crocodiles are sacred animals, for others they are not, but are treated on the contrary as enemies. Those who dwell around Thebes and around the lake of Moeris hold them to be most sacred, and each of these two peoples keeps one crocodile selected from the whole number, which has been trained to tameness. They put hanging ornaments of molten stone and of gold into its ears, and anklets round its front feet, and give it appointed food and sacrificial victims, and treat it as well as possible while it lives; and after it is dead they bury it in sacred tombs, embalming it. But those who dwell around the city of Elephantine even eat them, not holding them to be sacred. They are not called crocodiles but champsai; and the Ionians gave them the name of crocodile, comparing their form to that of the crocodiles (the lizards) that appear in their country in the stone walls.
